correctness.rationale: Finite backward reset ancestry supplies a unique finite-second-moment stationary law; the invariant linear Markov semigroup and stationary product-generator equations prove the exact two directional covariances. A strictly decreasing falling-factorial series characterizes a unique maximizer. Its controlled series expansion and uniform Poisson local limit give \(r t_j=j-2+O(j^{-1})\), a Gaussian front and \(j^{-1/2}\) maximal amplitude. Direct gamma integrals give time-integrated ratio \(2^j-1\). Standalone exact arithmetic and finite tests are supporting evidence, not substitutes for this proof.

The 2026 follow-up concerns transient one-time distributions and accumulation times; its accessible record does not give the claimed stationary two-time observables. No covering implication was found in the examined sources and accessible scientific finding summaries; full 2026 source inaccessible and stronger general linear-response coverage remain residual risks.

value.rationale: The motivating work treats information loss down a directed copying chain. Predicting when downstream measurements optimally recover an upstream signal, and how the best signal decays versus simultaneous observations, is a naturally motivated dynamical invariant. The exact Gaussian delay front, unique peak and directional integrated ratio give sharply distinguishable experimental/simulation benchmarks; they are not arbitrary integer or parameter slices.
